title: Sales enablement prospect kit: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch deck, pricing guidance, case studies, security FAQ
author: Alex Chen
content:
Overview

This prospect kit is a single-page reference sales enablement document for Standard / Enterprise prospects evaluating Redwood Inference. It combines concise positioning, competitive differentiation, a reproducible pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, exemplar case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for technical buyers. Use this during discovery, technical due diligence, and in pitch decks.

1) One-line positioning and elevator pitch

- Positioning (one-liner): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — backed by production-grade tooling for latency, reliability, and rollout control.
- Elevator pitch (30–60s): For engineering teams shipping LLM features at scale, Redwood provides a unified runtime and control plane that optimizes latency, cost, and operational reliability across cloud, reserved GPU pools, and private deployments. Unlike single-mode providers, Redwood gives teams consistent APIs, observability, and rollout controls so they can iterate quickly without rebuilding serving infrastructure.

2) Target buyer personas and key messages

- ML/Platform Engineer (primary): "I need predictable latency, throughput, and toolchain integration for model rollouts and KV cache management."
- Product Engineering / PM: "I want a simple API and SDKs that scale from prototype to production without re-architecting."
- Security/Compliance Lead: "I need deployment and data controls for regulated data and auditability."

Key messages per persona:
- ML/Platform: High-throughput runtime, automatic batching/caching, model/quantization recommendations, deterministic performance profiles.
- Product: Single API for hosted and private, fast SDK examples, canary/A-B rollouts built in.
- Security: VPC/private deploy options, KMS/HSM integration, detailed audit logs and SOC-ready evidence.

3) Top 6 differentiators (short bullets)

1. Production-first runtime: GPU-optimized serving, KV cache, continuous batching, and kernel selection tuned per workload.
2. Unified experience: same API, rollout, and observability across Hosted, Dedicated, Private deployments.
3. Cost controls: intelligent batching, caching, quant profiles and per-route cost dashboards.
4. Reliability: multi-tier fallbacks (model variants, region route), SLA-backed dedicated capacity.
5. Developer ergonomics: strong SDKs, quickstarts, prompt/eval-driven regressions.
6. Security & compliance: private control plane, KMS, audit logging, and documented evidence for audits.

4) Competitive brief (short table)

- Competitors considered: Large cloud AI platforms (managed model endpoints), LLM API-first providers, self-hosted inference runtimes/orchestration vendors.

Comparison table (high level):
| Dimension | Redwood | Cloud AI Platforms | LLM API Providers | Self-hosted Runtimes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment modes | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Hosted, some private via marketplace | Hosted only | Private only |
| Predictable throughput | Yes (Dedicated SLA) | Limited (ephemeral) | No | Depends on ops |
| Cost controls | Fine-grained (batching/caching/quant) | Limited | Minimal | Requires engineering |
| Observability / rollouts | Built-in dashboards & rollouts | Basic metrics | Limited | Varies |
| Security/compliance | VPC, KMS/HSM, audit evidence | Strong (cloud dependent) | Varies | Strong but self-managed |
| Time to production | Fast (API + templates) | Fast | Fast | Slow (ops) |

Positioning guidance vs major competitor types:
- Versus Cloud AI: emphasize consistent private deployment options, cost-optimization levers, and rollout controls.
- Versus API-only LLM: emphasize predictability at scale and Dedicated capacity SLAs.
- Versus self-hosted runtimes: emphasize managed observability, rollout tooling, and lower operational overhead.

5) Pitch deck outline (3–10 slides recommended for initial call)

1. Title / Intro: Customer name & quick objective (1 slide)
2. TL;DR: One-line value prop + 2–3 bullets on outcomes (cost reduction, latency SLOs, reliability) (1 slide)
3. Why now: market context and risks of DIY serving (1 slide)
4. How Redwood works: runtime + routing + deployment modes (1–2 slides)
5. Demo / integration: sample API call and quickstart time-to-first-request (code snippet) (1 slide)
6. Differentiation & proof points: Dedicated SLA, observability features, cost controls (1 slide)
7. Pricing & procurement: pricing tiers, reserved capacity examples, support levels (1 slide)
8. Customer stories / case studies (1 slide)
9. Security & compliance summary (1 slide)
10. Next steps & trial offer: POC plan and roles/owners (1 slide)

Snappy code snippet to include in slide 5 (short):
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
{
  "model": "open-llm-7b-v2",
  "prompt": "Summarize user message concisely",
  "max_tokens": 128
}

6) Pricing guidance (sales-facing rules of thumb)

- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token). Use customer metrics to estimate tokens/month. Example: 10M tokens/month -> estimate $X–$Y depending on model family and streaming ratio. (Provide exact quoting via pricing tool).
- Dedicated: committed monthly GPU capacity for predictable throughput. Typical entry point: 4–8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved with baseline throughput and burst policy. Provide example SKU pricing ranges in the quote tool.
- Private: platform licensing + optional support. Recommend 12–24 month enterprise contracts for air-gapped or regulated environments.

Pricing playbook bullets for SDRs/AEs:
1. Qualify model family (Llama-family / open-llm / customer custom) and expected tokens per call.
2. Estimate tokens/month and concurrency.
3. Recommend Hosted for <X tokens/month and non-sensitive data; Dedicated if predictability/throughput needed; Private for regulated data or on-prem requirements.
4. Offer 30–60 day POC with usage cap and sample performance benchmarks for enterprise deals.

7) Case studies (two short vignettes with measurable outcomes)

Case study A — Conversational support platform (SaaS startup)
- Situation: High concurrency chat API with latency requirement <200ms p95.
- Solution: Migrated from cloud managed endpoints to Redwood Dedicated with autoscale and KV prefix caching.
- Outcomes: Achieved p95 <180ms, 22% reduction in per-response cost via batching and caching, improved uptime to 99.95% during business hours.

Case study B — Regulated finance customer (mid-market)
- Situation: Sensitive PII, strict audit and key management needs.
- Solution: Private deployment in VPC with KMS integration and full audit logging; canary rollout for a custom risk-model.
- Outcomes: Passed internal audit, reduced average inference cost by 18% vs expensive cloud-hosted GPUs, enabled production rollout in 6 weeks.

8) Security FAQ for prospects (top 12 questions and concise answers)

Q1: Where does customer data reside?
A1: For Hosted, customer data resides in the selected cloud region with options to restrict regions; for Dedicated and Private, data remains within customer-dedicated pools or VPC/on-prem environments.

Q2: How is encryption handled?
A2: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+; data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. We offer KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private deployments.

Q3: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)?
A3: Yes — CMK and HSM integrations are available for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Q4: What audit logging is available?
A4: Request/response metadata, auth events, and admin actions are logged and can be shipped to customer SIEMs. We provide standardized SOC-style evidence packages on request.

Q5: How are access controls managed?
A5: RBAC with role groups, API keys, and SSO integration (OIDC/SAML). Admin console for role assignment and policy enforcement.

Q6: Can you run in air-gapped or on-prem environments?
A6: Yes — we offer an on-prem packaging option for Private deployments with documented installation and offline upgrade processes.

Q7: How do you handle model artifacts and provenance?
A7: Model versions are tracked in the control plane with checksums and provenance metadata. We support pinned model versions for each route.

Q8: What is your incident response and notification policy?
A8: We follow a documented incident response playbook with customer notification SLAs for security incidents. We provide a runbook and post-incident report for major events.

Q9: Are there penetration test and third-party audits?
A9: Yes — Redwood conducts regular third-party penetration tests and our audit reports (summaries) can be shared under NDA.

Q10: How do you protect against model exfiltration or data leakage?
A10: Controls include request/response filtering, configurable data retention policies, and optional runtime sandboxing in Private deployments. We also recommend canary/eval prompt sets for regression detection.

Q11: What compliance frameworks are supported?
A11: We provide evidence and controls aligned with SOC2; customers can request targeted compliance add-ons and guidance for HIPAA, GDPR, and regional data residency requirements.

Q12: Who is the security contact for enterprise onboarding?
A12: Security and compliance questions should be routed to security@redwood.ai (or your assigned solutions engineer).

9) Recommended POC plan (7 steps)

1. Discovery call (2–3 days): capture KPIs, latency targets, dataset sensitivity.
2. Proposal & scope (3–5 days): outline metrics, expected test cases, and access.
3. Sandbox access (day 0–2): provide hosted API keys + quickstart.
4. Baseline testing (week 1): run customer traffic simulation and metric collection.
5. Tune runbook (week 2): apply batching, caching, quantization suggestions.
6. Dedicated/Private pilot (week 3–6): optional Dedicated pool or Private deployment for realistic load.
7. Wrap & contract (week 6–8): present results and recommended sizing/commit.

10) Sales playbook snippets (operational tips for AEs/SEs)

- Ask early about tokens per request, concurrency, and data sensitivity.
- Use benchmark scripts from /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite to show expected latency/cost improvements.
- For procurement, route Dedicated and Private deals to enterprise contracting with finance/legal at week 4.
- Use security FAQ and SOC attestation artifacts during technical due diligence; escalate any NDA-required artifact requests to legal.
